office/kestrel-clock-spec.docx._note_numbering: The markers are the numbers Word shows, not a repeated '1.'. CommonMark takes a list's start from its FIRST marker and counts up on its own, so writing '1.' on every item was only correct while nothing ever split the list; the nested step is 2.1, so its own marker is 1 and the step after it is 3.
office/kestrel-clock-spec.docx._note_emphasis: The source bolds only the second half of the identifier (a plain run 'Dma' followed by a bold run 'ArbiterUnit'), which is how Word actually stores partial-word formatting. Faithful output is therefore 'Dma**ArbiterUnit**'. The tradeoff is deliberate and recorded in docs/quality-plan.md: the emphasis is real information the document carries, and markdown_to_text strips the markers before tokenizing, so the identifier is intact in the text layer the index and the KB consume. What is lost is a raw grep of document.md for the unsplit identifier.

pdf/kestrel-dataflow.pdf._note: XFAIL, and the marker is still the point: the ROUTING bug is fixed, the document is not. As of 2026-09-26 `pdf_has_text_layer` judges a thin window by the PDF's own objects, so this diagram-only DIGITAL page (79 chars/page, 12 vector paths, no raster) is no longer misrouted to full-document OCR -- it converts through the digital path and its real text layer is measured (`pdf-text-coverage`, token_recall 1.0 over 13 source tokens, absent 0). What remains broken is the CONVERSION: docling's layout model finds no picture at all in a vector-only page, so nothing is extracted, `images.gate` reads `pass` over ZERO images, `content.headings` is 0, and the whole document is 19 tokens of the diagram's labels run together as one line. `status: ok` over that is a vacuous pass -- a recall of 1.0 against the 13 tokens the page happens to hold says nothing about the diagram nobody extracted. The keys below therefore pin what this lane MUST return: a document that admits it is degraded and names the figure it could not bring through. Encoding today's `status: ok, images_gate: pass` would make the eval assert that a destroyed document is fine, which is the one thing it exists to refuse. Remaining fixes, both M1: extract figures on a page whose content is vector art (docling's picture detection owns this, and a floor may have to come from the PDF's own drawing clusters); and stop `images.gate` reading `pass` over zero images, which is the same vacuity as a recall of 1.0 over no tokens. office/kestrel-ligature.docx._note: The OFFICE half of the character-layer fixture, and its job is to be BORING. The source holds literal ligature glyphs (U+FB00/FB01/FB02/FB03) and a soft hyphen; the office gate must be blind to all of them, because both its sides read the same OOXML and the shared tokenizer treats a ligature identically wherever it appears. Recall is exactly 1.0 and `normalize_pdf_text` is NOT in this path -- if it ever were, this row is what would notice. `md_contains` asserts the glyphs survive into the markdown VERBATIM: folding them here would be a silent rewrite of the document's own characters, which is Job 1's whole prohibition. The PDF derived from this same file is where the fold earns its keep -- see pdf/kestrel-ligature.pdf.

pdf/kestrel-ligature.pdf._note: MEASURED TRUTH, and it pins two different things at once. (1) THE FOLD WORKS: every ligature the source spells with U+FB01 (fi) or U+FB02 (fl) -- configuration, field, confirms, classification, fixed, final, flushes, first, confidential, flow, profiling -- is COVERED, because `normalize_pdf_text` folds both sides before they are compared. Measured on this document with the fold removed, recall is 0.7976 over 84 source tokens; with it, 0.9041 over 73. Without the fold this document sits BELOW `min_recall` (0.8), so the fold is the difference between a document that reports content loss and one that does not. (2) A REAL DOCLING DEFECT, pinned rather than hidden: the 7 tokens still absent are offset x2, offsets, affinity, difficult, efficient, ffer -- every one of them a word the source spells with U+FB00 (ff) or U+FB03 (ffi). docling drops or MISPLACES those glyphs (its markdown reads 'o set flow' and 'hyphen ff ation' where the source reads 'offset flow' and 'hyphenation'), while the fi/fl glyphs come through. `gap_absent_max: 7` is therefore a CEILING on a known converter bug, not a target: it falls when docling handles ff/ffi, and any rise means a new one. The row is not `xfail` -- nothing here is vacuous, the number is honest and the document is otherwise healthy.
